subject: Scope & Timing for Privacy Event — Evidence Access & Subprocessor Inventory
messages:
From: Brian Holt <security@finexinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops (Finex) <legal@finexinc.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Suspicious access — initial ask for scope and export ETA

Hi Marissa / Olga,

We detected anomalous read activity on a small set of customer records in our test tenancy that reference data processed via Redwood. We don't believe this is a wide-scale exfil, but we need to lock down the scope and get an encrypted slice of relevant logs and any mapping to Redwood-subprocessor exports.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood saw any reads or exports tied to the tenant id FINEX-0091 between 2026-12-13 22:00 UTC and 2026-12-14 03:00 UTC.
- If yes, provide an ETA for a minimally-scoped evidence export (audit log snippet + object mapping). We need chain-of-custody metadata and a pointer to the subprocessor inventory used for that tenant.

We are escalating internally; Legal wants to know if an emergency evidence-access authorization (DocuSign) is required from Finex to proceed. I can attach an encrypted sample of the relevant audit entries.

Attached: audit-snippet-20261214.json.enc

Thanks,
Brian
Security Incident Response Lead
Finex Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Brian Holt <security@finexinc.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious access — initial ask for scope and export ETA

Brian — thanks for the heads up and for the encrypted snippet. We’ll treat this as a high-priority incident.

Quick plan and asks:
- Olga will run the access audit against FINEX-0091 for the window you specified and confirm whether any Redwood-initiated exports occurred. Target ETA for a scoped audit export: 4 hours (14:00 PST) — we’ll push sooner if we find relevant records.
- We need Finex to sign an emergency evidence-access authorization if the export contains customer-identifying payloads. If Legal prefers, we can accept a signed DocuSign envelope; Brian, please confirm the signed contact and I'll share the DocuSign link.
- Please provide the list of external IPs / actor IDs you are tracking; it speeds correlation.
- Naomi: please pull the current subprocessor inventory row for FINEX-0091 and attach a CSV snapshot to the thread (I referenced our internal template). Ben: can you prep a manifest that maps audit event ids -> storage objects and any retention tags (S3 prefixes / retention policy).

Attachments planned from Redwood: redwood_subproc_inventory_20261214.csv (Naomi) and manifest_export_FINEX-0091.zip (Ben, outbound once scoped).

If we confirm an export is necessary and contains PII, we will follow our documented chain-of-custody and hash the artifacts before transfer. I’ve opened INC0012345 in our tracking system and will update it with deliverables and timestamps.

Next steps: Olga to confirm access results within 4 hours.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: SecAck Team <sec-ack@finexinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops (Finex) <legal@finexinc.com>, Brian Holt <security@finexinc.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 12:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious access — initial ask for scope and export ETA

Marissa — thanks. We can provision a signed emergency authorization within 30 minutes if you send the DocuSign link. Attaching an encrypted audit excerpt here so you can pre-check for identifiers.

We are tracking two external actor IPs (198.51.100.22, 203.0.113.11). The actors appear to have accessed three objects that reference user_email fields; those might be partial hashes, we need your confirmation on whether those were materialized by Redwood during the processing pipeline.

Attachment: audit-snippet-20261214.json.enc

Also — please confirm whether a subprocessor pull will include timestamps in UTC and whether we can request a limited export (IDs + hashes) to speed triage. If Redwood needs our signature to unlock the full export, send the DocuSign envelope link to sec-ack@finexinc.com and legal@finexinc.com.

Regards,
Finex Security Acknowledgements Team
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Brian Holt <security@finexinc.com>, SecAck Team <sec-ack@finexinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 15:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious access — initial ask for scope and export ETA

Thanks all — quick status:
- I ran a targeted audit for tenant FINEX-0091 across the window you provided. No Redwood-initiated export jobs were scheduled in that timeframe. We did observe read activity on intermediate processing buckets tied to our feature-store (access by internal worker role), which I'll include in a scoped artifact.
- Naomi attached the current subprocessor snapshot here: redwood_subproc_inventory_20261214.csv (contains the processors used by FINEX-0091).
- Ben will prepare a manifest that maps the observed audit event ids to S3 objects and retention tags; ETA: 2 hours.

We will prepare a minimized export (IDs + UTC timestamps + object paths + cryptographic hashes) and provide a signed hash manifest for chain-of-custody. If Finex signs the emergency authorization, we will attach the full encrypted export (payload allowed only to Finex legal).

For transparency, here is the internal runbook link (read-only) we will follow: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-finex-evidence

Action items:
- Finex to send DocuSign envelope for emergency evidence access (sec-ack@finexinc.com & legal@finexinc.com).
- Ben to deliver manifest_export_FINEX-0091.zip (2h).
- Marissa to post chain-of-custody hashes to INC0012345 when export is ready.

Olga Petrov
Sr. Incident Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference
